summary: Verified new throughput / rate-limit / idempotency / Slack-OAuth requirements. All 18 backend pytest tests pass (1 skipped: no failed jobs to retry). Key new tests: (a) Rate-limit reschedule with hourlyLimit=2 + 5 recipients yields exactly 2 sent, 3 scheduled with rescheduledForRateLimit=true, 0 failed; (b) No-duplicate-send with 3 recipients yields 3 unique sends each with previewUrl and stable sent count on repeat reads; (c) GET /api/auth/slack/oauth/start returns 501 with error.code=NOT_CONFIGURED (no crash); (d) GET /api/auth/config returns slackOAuthConfigured=false, supabaseConfigured present, devLoginEnabled=true. Regression: dev-login, /me (401 without token), scheduled/sent pagination, stats, search, retry 409 on non-failed, real Ethereal E2E send, Slack webhook connect/status/disconnect all still pass. Frontend Settings verified: slack-webhook-input + slack-connect present, slack-oauth-connect NOT rendered (since slackOAuthConfigured=false), SLACK_CLIENT_ID hint visible, connect->disconnect flow works end-to-end.
critical_code_review_comments: Idempotency correctly implemented via atomic updateMany({where:{status:'scheduled'}}) claim in email.worker.ts — safe under WORKER_CONCURRENCY>1.
Rate-limit reschedule path preserves status='scheduled' + sets rescheduledForRateLimit=true and re-enqueues via BullMQ with jobId suffix rl:<window> (no drops, no fails, restart-safe).
Slack OAuth start returns 501+NOT_CONFIGURED via AppError instead of crashing — graceful degradation confirmed.
rateLimit.service.ts uses atomic Redis INCR with per-hour windowed keys and decrements on over-limit; TTL slightly exceeds window — correct.
email.service.ts enforces delayMs>=MIN_EMAIL_DELAY_MS and hourlyLimit>=1; scheduled offsets start+i*delayMs — correct.
test_credentials: Dev sign-in via POST /api/auth/dev-login {} (optionally {email:'x@...'} for a fresh sender). UI: 'Continue with Google' (data-testid=google-signin-button).
seed_data_creation: Each rate-limit / idempotency test uses a fresh sender email (rltest+<uuid>@reachinbox.ai / idem+<uuid>@reachinbox.ai) so the per-sender Redis hourly counter starts clean.
context_for_next_testing_agent: For rate-limit tests, ALWAYS use a unique dev-login email — Redis hourly counter persists per sender per hour. Rate-limit reschedule test needs ~15-30s wait since last recipient's initial scheduledAt is start+(n-1)*delayMs; poll until sent==2 AND rescheduledForRateLimit-flagged==3. Slack OAuth 501 is by design (SLACK_CLIENT_ID/SECRET unset in this env) — not a bug.
rca of the issue: No production issues. Test flake fixed by extending the rate-limit assertion wait to 45s (was 30s) and polling until both sent==2 AND flagged==3, since the 5th recipient is only enqueued 8s after schedule time.
